$comment: The repository's tool-permission list, rendered by community/.ai/render-guides.mjs into
Edit this file and rerun `bazel run //.ai:render-guides`; never edit the generated
Entries are argv prefixes, not command strings: ["./bazel.cmd", "build"] matches
`./bazel.cmd build //x` but never `./bazel.cmd clean`. Both matchers compare literal text, so a
leading `./` is emitted in both spellings; other spellings of the same file (`../../x`, an
absolute path) fall through to a prompt.
This list says nothing about *where* a command may point, and cannot: a prefix match sees argv,
not paths, so `ls`, `cat`, `stat` and the rest below are allowed for every path on the machine.
Which paths are in scope is the guide's Tooling rules, not this file. Narrowing that here would
mean dropping those commands outright, which prompts on every `out/` and `idea.log` read.
Each harness matches every stage of a pipeline independently, which is why the read-only
filters at the end of `allow` are listed at all: without them `rg.cmd x | head -5` prompts.
`deny` wins over `allow` in both harnesses and is the load-bearing half: it also overrides
Claude Code's built-in read-only command set, which is what `grep` and `find` are listed for.
`{{TOOLS_DIR}}` resolves per edition (./community/tools, or ./tools in a community checkout).
Everything else is spelled relative to the workspace root the rules are rendered into.
$comment_deny: `grep` and `find` are denied outright, in every pipeline position: pipe into
`{{TOOLS_DIR}}/rg.cmd` instead, which reads stdin. Expressing "denied only as the first stage"
took a whole argv-parsing hook; the flat rule is what lets both harnesses do this natively.
$comment_denyTools: Whole tools, denied by name. Claude Code drops these from the model's context entirely, so no
call is attempted; the guide's Tooling rules point at the ijproxy and rg.cmd/fd.cmd equivalents.
Codex has no such tools, so its rules file omits this section.
$comment_additionalDirectories: Directories outside the workspace that Claude Code treats as working directories. A session

nothing. `EnterWorktree` into a lease asks every time, and neither an allow rule nor a hook
removes that prompt, because the pool is outside `.claude/worktrees/`. A pool that
